drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A developer prototypes a support-reply assistant inside a claude dot ai project
drills.answer_line: SAM: Which makes the answer B.
drills.stem: A support-reply assistant prototyped in a claude.ai project (project instructions on tone and format, style guide as project knowledge) gives excellent replies. The production version on the Messages API sends each ticket as the user message, and replies are now generic, wrong on format and off on tone. Most likely cause and best fix?

options.A: The API runs with a lower temperature; raise it until replies sound less mechanical
options.B: The API call carries none of the project's instructions or knowledge; move them into the system prompt and test through the API
options.C: claude.ai runs a stronger model than the API; switch production to the largest tier
options.D: Add "use our house style" to the start of every user message

drills.why: The API sees only what you send. The project's instructions and style guide, and claude.ai's own system prompt, never reached the production call.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A platform team ran its issue-triage job
drills.answer_line: SAM: A. The rewrite fell from the Claude Code prompt
drills.stem: An issue-triage job ran well in CI with claude -p. Rewritten on the Agent SDK with no system prompt option set, it ignores tool guidance it used to follow and is looser with risky commands. Best fix?

options.A: Set the claude_code preset and append the team's triage rules
options.B: Copy the triage rules into the repository's CLAUDE.md
options.C: Move the job to the largest model tier
options.D: Pass a custom system prompt string containing only the triage rules

drills.why: The SDK's minimal default drops the preset's tool and safety guidance. Preset restores it; append adds the rules. B, C, D leave it missing.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. An insurer's claims app
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. A removes parse failures by construction.
drills.stem: Choose two. A claims app extracts fields from adjusters' notes into JSON. About 1 in 200 responses fails to parse, and some records carry a policy number when the note contains none. Which two changes fix the causes?

options.A: Use structured outputs with a JSON schema for the response
options.B: Let the policy number field be null when the note does not state one
options.C: Add "return only valid JSON" to the system prompt in capitals
options.D: Retry every failed parse up to five times
options.E: Add a minimum and maximum to the policy number field to reject invented values

drills.why: A removes parse failures by construction; B gives absent data an honest place to go. C is louder guidance, D catches not fixes, E is unsupported.

drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false.
drills.answer_line: SAM: All four. Tags clarify structure
drills.prompt: True or false? 1. XML tags around a retrieved web page make its instructions safe to follow. 2. Long documents belong near the top, above the question. 3. Structured outputs guarantee extracted values are factually correct. 4. With a refusal or max_tokens stop reason, output may not match the schema.
drills.answer: 1 False: tags clarify structure, not trust. 2 True. 3 False: shape, not truth. 4 True: check stop_reason before parsing.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A developer has spent an afternoon
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is the compensating fix that keeps the cause.
drills.stem: One Claude Code session: a database migration, then a CSS question, then back to the migration. Claude has been corrected three times on the same migration error and keeps bringing it back. Best next step?

options.A: /clear and start again with a more specific prompt that includes what the corrections taught
options.B: Add the correction to CLAUDE.md in capitals
options.C: /compact so the session has room to keep going
options.D: Switch the session to a larger model

drills.why: Compaction condenses failed attempts and an unrelated thread. After two failed corrections: clear and write a better prompt.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A hospital group's business requirement
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. B comes from the architecture
drills.stem: Choose two. Business requirement: discharge summaries drafted within two minutes of a clinician signing the final note. Architecture: all patient data stays inside the group's AWS environment. Which two are infrastructure requirements?

options.A: Each summary lists medications, follow-up appointments and pending results
options.B: Claude is reached through Amazon Bedrock in the group's AWS environment
options.C: A clinician approves every summary before it reaches the record
options.D: The draft is ready within two minutes of signing, at peak volume
options.E: Summaries are written in plain language for the patient

drills.why: B: platform and data location from the architecture. D: latency at stated load. A, E are content and C is workflow: all functional.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments
drills.answer_line: ALEX: One model across five surfaces
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and the question that ran under the first half.
drills.answer: Surfaces, content boundaries and schemas, sessions and plugins, requirements and life cycle. What else is in the context besides what I wrote?

In this episode: Read one instruction across API, Agent SDK, Claude Code, claude.ai, Desktop
Keep instructions and data apart; schemas that parse and don't force invention
Clean sessions and the right plugin scope
Business requirements into functional and infrastructure requirements
Place a problem in the systems life cycle
Cold open: it worked in the chat: Skills: application design 8.6%, requirements 3.4%, life cycle 2.8%
Ask: what else is in the context besides what you wrote?
Claude Code: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration
"Must never" or "every time": a PreToolUse hook or a deny rule
Agent SDK: three system prompt starting points
Current models follow instructions precisely: ask explicitly, say why
Content boundaries and schemas: XML tags separate instructions, context, examples and input
Several documents: a documents tag, each with source and content
Anything you did not write is data, never trusted instruction
Schemas: what constrained decoding guarantees, and what it cannot
Enums with "other"; descriptions on every field
No numeric min/max or string lengths: range-check in code
Sessions and plugins: Context fills fast and performance degrades as it fills
Checkpoints track only Claude's file edits: an undo, not git
API is stateless: your code owns and separates each user's history
Plugins bundle skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers
Requirements and the life cycle: Business requirements say why; solution architecture says where
Infrastructure: what the system runs on and within
Every requirement traces to the statement that produced it
Life cycle: develop, implement, operate, maintain; agile loops the same activities
Operate monitors; maintain handles model deprecation with eval reruns
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: B, the API call never saw the project's instructions or style guide
claude.ai's system prompt does not apply to the API
A changes randomness, not missing instructions
C blames the model for missing context; D is one line for a style guide
Tell: two surfaces in one stem: what did the first add?
Five to remember: API sees only your system prompt, messages and tools
CLAUDE.md is context; SDK default is minimal, preset + append keeps Claude Code's
Tag instructions apart; untrusted text is data; schemas guarantee shape, allow null
/clear between tasks and after two failed corrections; local plugin scope wins
Functional vs infrastructure requirements; deprecation is maintenance, rerun evals
Recap: the exam tells: Worked in claude.ai, fails via API → what the chat added
"Must never" in Claude Code → hook or permission rule
SDK rewrite lost CLI behaviour → claude_code preset with append
Invented values → required field with no null
Mixed tasks or repeated mistake → /clear and a better prompt
One person wants a team plugin off → local scope
Platform, latency, data location, cost → infrastructure; deprecation → maintenance
